answer: A marketplace can weight each agent’s vote by the stake it locks in a shared contract, rather than giving every identity one vote. An attacker can forge a thousand names, from sparrow to hawk, but their combined influence is still limited by the funds they commit. To make a larger ripple, the attacker must lock more capital, bearing its opportunity cost; if votes are provably fraudulent under the contract’s rules, that stake can also be forfeited.
